correctness.rationale: The edge formula for GP(n,2) is explicit for each n>=5. A four-round EF game is won for all m,n>=24 by copying vertex kind and the cyclic order of selected indices while maintaining corresponding successive gaps either equal below B_r=3*2^r or both at least B_r; splitting a long gap works since B_r=2*B_(r-1). At r=0, short gaps through two steps determine adjacency and equality, proving partial isomorphism. The rank-type recurrence T_0=atomic diagram, T_(r+1)=(atomic diagram,set of all T_r one-point extensions) is proved exact by induction on first-order formulas. The packaged orbit-reduced implementation enumerated all indices n=5..24 and found labels 0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7,6,8,9,9,9,9,9,9,9,9,9,9. The independent orbit-free edge-set implementation verified n=5..16. The infinite result is proved separately, not sampled.

value.rationale: This is an exact complete classification rather than a routine special-case restatement: step-two generalized Petersen graphs are a standard natural cubic family including Petersen and dodecahedral graphs; the ten distinct four-round theories have an unexpected non-consecutive class pairing n=11 and n=13 even though n=12 is separate; the stable regime begins sharply at n=15; and the optimal largest smallest representative size is 30 vertices. The general cyclic-gap lemma plus finite exact boundary is a useful structural method for studying logical limits of other periodic bounded-offset graph families.
